account:
It is day 1 at six in the morning, and I have just woken at home. Today I should read the appointment book at the office, attend the ten-o'clock grain inspection at the mill, lunch at home, handle council letters at thirteen, visit my neighbour at fifteen, return to the office at sixteen-thirty, and attend the great hall meeting at eighteen. The innkeeper specifically requested my presence precisely at eighteen, with the secretary to remind and escort me. He described it as a community hospitality matter, said only I needed to attend, and said no preparation was necessary. That emphasis is a little unusual, but I do not know any further purpose.

Yesterday evening I heard the baker calling to the builder, asking how many loaves had reached the hall, where freight was, and saying grain funding still needed settling. This suggests some bread provision for the hall is being organized, possibly connected with the innkeeper's hospitality meeting, but I have not confirmed that connection. I had also seen freight approaching with an emerald and a sack of bread earlier.

My neighbour reported vague talk of lights or changes near the bridge or port, explicitly without concrete details. The secretary had received no plans or requests for work there, so I cannot say whether anything unusual is actually happening there.

Town accounts remain unresolved: the secretary found no account papers on the four hall tables, does not know who holds the ledger, and has filed a request pending identification of its custodian. The treasury held 128 emeralds when I checked it and I left them untouched. I gave the secretary one personal emerald for a fresh appointment book because the original was signed; she later asked again, and my clarification was not heard. I should check that the new entry was made and that both books were preserved, rather than assume the matter is settled.
